mbm-0368.clue: I lost the castle. The horse is safe.
mbm-0368.quote: Our wooden game castle split at the corner. I made a little paddock from the broken walls and put the horse inside. We now have to negotiate with a farmer to finish the game.

mbm-0369.clue: I found the city in a spoon rack.
mbm-0369.quote: At the market a stallholder had souvenir spoons from every neighborhood. I picked the one with the little fountain and followed her directions. The fountain was exactly the size of the picture in my hand, until I walked up close.

mbm-0370.clue: I took the shoes for a walk first.
mbm-0370.quote: On my sightseeing day I followed a line of painted yellow footprints on the pavement. They led to a cobbler, who pointed me to the oldest street in town and offered to polish the evidence.

mbm-0371.clue: I put the crumbs on afterward.
mbm-0371.quote: I made a patchwork toast rack for the breakfast quilt. Mum said the display looked much too neat, so I embroidered three brown crumbs under the smallest slice. Now it looks like our table.

mbm-0372.clue: I wrote the color of the door first.
mbm-0372.quote: Before my first skydive I was so nervous that all I could remember was the orange plane door. After the canopy opened I could see a hundred fields below. I filled the rest of the notebook page in green.

mbm-0373.clue: I learned to turn from the fringe.
mbm-0373.quote: My cousin’s shawl swung out just before every turn in our folk dance. I watched the fringe until my feet knew what to do. Last week a new dancer watched my sleeves the same way.

mbm-0374.clue: My robot works the night shift.
mbm-0374.quote: I wired a pinprick light into the garage window on my mecha display. Switch off the room light and the whole machine is just a giant shadow visiting one tiny mechanic.

mbm-0375.clue: I started with the orange thumb.
mbm-0375.quote: Paint spilled on my thumb while I was trying to mix a sunset. I pressed it to a scrap and painted the whole harbor around that little orange sun. I kept the thumbprint ridges.

mbm-0376.clue: I keep the lane rope for a bookmark.
mbm-0376.quote: Our pool replaced its lane dividers and gave us the little bits of cord at the ends. I cut a blue piece for my swim log and knotted it beside the day I first did ten lengths.

mbm-0377.clue: I go out dancing for the first ten seconds.
mbm-0377.quote: Our DJ begins my favorite song very quietly. For those ten seconds you can hear every shoe turn toward the floor. That rustle of a whole room deciding to dance gets me every time.

mbm-0378.quote: My mum kept embroidered pillowcases from several different houses. I quilted a roof over each spray of flowers, so all the old windows could look out on the same street.

mbm-0379.clue: I sit beside the aisle lamp.
mbm-0379.quote: The old cinema lights the aisle with a lamp shaped like a seashell. I used to think a real shell made that warm pink light. I still choose the seat where it glows by my knee.

mbm-0380.clue: I know the mountain by its buttons.
mbm-0380.quote: My hiking jacket has a different button from each friend who has mended it on the trail. The wooden one comes from our wettest climb. It still swells a little when the mist comes in.

mbm-0381.quote: My little brother likes the smell of citrus at his study desk. I crocheted an orange around a tiny bag of dried peel. Squeeze the wool and the whole room smells like his lunchbox.

mbm-0382.clue: I always ask for an empty saucer.
mbm-0382.quote: My coin trick ends with a silver piece clinking into a porcelain saucer. When I practiced at my aunt’s house, her cat came running for every clink. The cat is now my final surprise.

mbm-0383.clue: I keep the little brass anchor upside down.
mbm-0383.quote: I stamped an anchor into a leather luggage tag, then noticed I’d put it inside out. When the tag flips in a breeze the anchor looks perfectly upright. My brother says it knows when we’re traveling.

mbm-0384.clue: I read the last paragraph on the steps.
mbm-0384.quote: I was halfway home from the bookshop when I reached the good part. I sat on the library steps until I finished, and a librarian brought me a cushion without asking a single question.

mbm-0385.clue: We gave the microphone a bicycle basket.
mbm-0385.quote: Our band needed somewhere to keep spare picks at rehearsals. I clipped my old bike basket onto the microphone stand. It now holds picks, a tambourine and the front-door key nobody can ever find.

mbm-0386.clue: I found the binoculars before the bird.
mbm-0386.quote: I wiped the rain off the lenses and saw a second, tiny reflection of a red-headed bird on the glass. I turned around and there it was on the fence, waiting for me to look the obvious way.

mbm-0387.clue: I draw the station lamps with a white pencil.
mbm-0387.quote: I take dark paper to the platform at dusk. I can fill a whole page with glowing windows before the train arrives. The engine’s single headlamp is the last mark I make.

mbm-0388.clue: I crocheted my own umbrella handle.
mbm-0388.quote: The cover is blue wool with little yellow stars. When I’m waiting for the bus all the umbrellas look alike from above, but my hand knows which one is mine.

mbm-0389.clue: Our anime club has a three-second orchestra.
mbm-0389.quote: We paused a little festival scene and each chose one instrument we could see. At our next meeting we tried to make the sound ourselves. My rice tin played a surprisingly good drum roll.

mbm-0390.clue: I made the handle for a left thumb.
mbm-0390.quote: I shaped a mug for my left-handed uncle and pressed a resting spot into the clay with my own left thumb. He picked it up without looking at the handle, and his thumb went exactly where I hoped.

mbm-0391.clue: I went out to count blue doors.
mbm-0391.quote: A guide mentioned the hill’s famous blue doors, so I tried to count them. I stopped at seven because the seventh opened onto a courtyard full of dancing paper lanterns. Seven was plenty.

mbm-0392.clue: I keep a drawing of my first footprint.
mbm-0392.quote: After my first martial-arts forms class I stepped off the mat with a damp heel and left a perfect print. My teacher traced it in chalk to mark where I’d started. That chalk line outlasted all my nerves.
